questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This tests practical security tooling integration and explains how to enforce image signing early.

## Key Concepts
- Image signing with cosign
- Manifest parsing to collect images
- CI integration (GitHub Actions) and local validation

## Code Example
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
PUBKEY=${COSIGN_PUBLIC_KEY:-cosign.pub}
for f in manifests/**/*.yaml; do
  images=$(yq e '.. | .image? // empty' "$f" 2>/dev/null)
  for img in $images; do
    cosign verify --key "$PUBKEY" "$img" || { echo "Unsigned: $img"; exit 1; }
  done
done
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle dynamic image tags vs. digests in this gate?
- How would you test the workflow locally before opening a PR?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

In production Kubernetes environments, ensuring supply-chain security for Helm-based deployments is critical. This question evaluates your ability to integrate multiple security tools—Helm templating, SBOM generation, and image signature verification—into a cohesive CI gate. It tests practical knowledge of enforcing provenance and attestations before code merges.

## Key Concepts

- **Helm templating and values extraction**: Rendering charts to discover all container images referenced in deployments
- **SBOM generation**: Using Syft to create a CycloneDX SBOM that catalogs all dependencies and artifacts
- **Image signing verification**: Using cosign to validate container image signatures against a public key stored in the repository
- **CI gate integration**: Implementing fail-fast behavior in GitHub Actions to block unsigned images and missing attestations

## Code Example

```yaml
# Minimal GitHub Actions workflow for Helm image signing enforcement
name: Helm Image Security Gate

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  helm-security:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install cosign
        uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v3

      - name: Install Helm and Syft
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/helm/helm/main/scripts/get-helm-3 | bash
          curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anchore/syft/main/install.sh | sh

      - name: Render Helm templates
        run: helm template my-app ./chart --values values.yaml --output-dir ./rendered

      - name: Extract image references
        run: |
          grep -rh 'image:' ./rendered | awk '{print $2}' > images.txt

      - name: Generate SBOM with Syft
        run: |
          syft $(cat images.txt) -o cyclonedx-json > sbom.json

      - name: Verify image signatures with cosign
        run: |
          COSIGN_PUBLIC_KEY=cosign.pub
          for IMAGE in $(cat images.txt); do
            cosign verify --key $COSIGN_PUBLIC_KEY $IMAGE || exit 1
          done
```

## Why This Is Asked

## Key Concepts

- Policy-as-code (OPA, Kyverno)
- Runtime security (Falco/eBPF)
- Multi-tenant governance and testability

## Code Example

```javascript
// OPA Rego (conceptual)
package kubernetes.admission
violation[reason] {
  input.review.object.kind == "Pod"
  image := input.review.object.spec.containers[_].image
  not imageIsAttested(image)
  reason = "image provenance missing"
}
```

```javascript
// Kyverno policy (conceptual)
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-provenance-and-security
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
  - name: require-nonroot
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Pod"]
    validate:
      message: "must set runAsNonRoot and readOnlyRootFilesystem"
      pattern:
        spec:
          containers:
          - securityContext:
              runAsNonRoot: true
  - name: require-attested-image
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Pod"]
    validate:
      message: "image must have Rekor cosign attestation"
      pattern:
        spec:
          containers:
          - image: "*attested*"
```

```javascript
// Falco rule (conceptual)
- rule: Unsigned Image Usage
  condition: container.image.signature == ""
  output: "Unsigned image detected: %container.image.repository"
  priority: WARN
```

## Why This Is Asked

## Code Example
```yaml
# Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate sketch (simplified)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: gputypematch
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: GPUsTypeConstraint
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package gputypematch
      violation["msg"] = msg :-
        input.review.object.kind == "Pod"
        and some container in input.review.object.spec.containers
        and container.resources.requests["nvidia.com/gpu"] > 0
        and not input.review.object.spec.nodeSelector["gpuType"] in allowed_types
        and not input.review.object.metadata.namespace in namespace_allowlist
        msg := "GPU type not allowed in namespace"
```

## Why This Is Asked

This evaluates the ability to translate security requirements into automated validation for Helm-rendered Kubernetes manifests, demonstrating practical DevOps security implementation skills.

## Key Concepts

- Helm template rendering for manifest generation
- Kubernetes container securityContext enforcement
- GitHub Actions as CI/CD security gates
- Lightweight YAML validation using shell scripting

## Code Example

```yaml
# Minimal GitHub Actions workflow
name: Helm Security Gate
on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - 'charts/**'
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - uses: actions/setup-helm@v3
      - name: Render and validate security context
        run: |
          helm template myapp charts/myapp > rendered.yaml
          # Validate security context fields
          python3 scripts/validate-security.py rendered.yaml
```

```python
# scripts/validate-security.py
import sys, yaml
with open(sys.argv[1]) as f:
    docs = yaml.safe_load_all(f)
for doc in docs:
    if doc.get('kind') == 'Deployment':
        for container in doc['spec']['template']['spec']['containers']:
            ctx = container.get('securityContext', {})
            if not ctx.get('runAsNonRoot'):
                print(f"FAIL: {container['name']} missing runAsNonRoot")
                sys.exit(1)
            if not ctx.get('runAsUser', 0) >= 1000:
                print(f"FAIL: {container['name']} runAsUser < 1000")
                sys.exit(1)
            if not ctx.get('readOnlyRootFilesystem'):
                print(f"FAIL: {container['name']} missing readOnlyRootFilesystem")
                sys.exit(1)
print("All security context checks passed")
```

```yaml
# Failing Helm template - missing readOnlyRootFilesystem
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: myapp
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:latest
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 1000
          # readOnlyRootFilesystem: true  # Missing - will fail CI
```

```yaml
# Passing Helm template - complete security context
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: myapp
spec:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:latest
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 1000
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
```

## Verification

**Local testing:**
```bash
helm template myapp charts/myapp | python3 scripts/validate-security.py -
```

**CI verification:** The GitHub Actions workflow runs automatically on pull requests, rendering templates and validating security context fields before allowing merge.

## Why This Question Is Asked

This question evaluates the ability to design end-to-end secure supply chain controls in a real-world, multi-region, multi-tenant Kubernetes environment. It assesses understanding of image signing, policy-as-code enforcement, cross-registry workflows, CI/CD integration, runtime protection mechanisms, and signing key rotation strategies.

## Key Concepts

- **Sigstore Cosign and Rekor**: Provide transparent, audit-logged image signing and verification through a public transparency log, eliminating the need for managing traditional signing keys.
- **Image provenance and attestations**: Deliver cryptographic proof of image origin and build process, ensuring containers originate from trusted sources.
- **Digest pinning**: Prevents tag-based attacks by binding deployments to specific immutable image digests rather than mutable tags.
- **Keyless signing**: Uses OIDC identities (GitHub Actions, Google, Microsoft) for authentication, simplifying key rotation and reducing secret sprawl.
- **Admission controllers**: Kyverno or OPA Gatekeeper intercept API requests at admission time, enforcing policy before workloads schedule.

## Security Properties Enforced

| Control | Threat Mitigated |
|---|---|
| Cosign signature verification | Unauthorized image deployment |
| Rekor transparency log | Signing key compromise or repudiation |
| Digest pinning | Tag swap attacks, registry compromise |
| readOnlyRootFilesystem | Container filesystem manipulation |
| runAsNonRoot | Privilege escalation via root |
| noPrivilegeEscalation | Container breakout attempts |

## Multi-Tenant Considerations

For multi-tenant clusters, apply ClusterPolicies with namespace-level exceptions using `generate` rules or leverage OPA's `data.kubernetes.namespace` for tenant-specific policies. Consider combining with admission control annotations for tenant-controlled image allowlists while maintaining platform-wide baseline security.

## Alternatives to Kyverno

OPA Gatekeeper with ConstraintTemplates offers equivalent functionality for teams already invested in the OPA ecosystem, providing Rego-based policy authoring with familiar tooling and broader ecosystem support.

## Why This Is Asked

This question tests foundational secure supply chain practices in a beginner-friendly manner. It mirrors real-world CI gates used in production environments around Dockerfile hygiene, image signing, SBOM generation, and registry controls. It introduces modern tools like Cosign and SBOM attestations without overwhelming complexity.

## Key Concepts

- **Dockerfile Hygiene**: Non-root USER and multi-stage builds reduce security vulnerabilities and image size
- **Container Image Signing**: Using Cosign to sign and verify container images ensures integrity
- **SBOM Attestation**: Software Bill of Materials provides transparency into image contents and dependencies
- **GitHub Actions Workflows**: Implementing gates and policy checks in CI/CD pipelines
- **Registry Allowlist**: Restricting deployments to approved registries prevents supply chain attacks

## Code Example

```yaml
# Minimal GitHub Actions workflow
name: Docker Security Gate
on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      
      - name: Validate Dockerfile
        run: |
          # Check for non-root USER
          grep -q 'USER ' Dockerfile || exit 1
          # Check for multi-stage build
          grep -q 'FROM.*AS' Dockerfile || exit 1
      
      - name: Build and push image
        run: |
          docker build -t ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/app:${{ github.sha }} .
          docker push ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/app:${{ github.sha }}
      
      - name: Generate SBOM
        run: |
          syft ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/app:${{ github.sha }} -o spdx-json > sbom.json
      
      - name: Sign image and SBOM with Cosign
        run: |
          cosign sign ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/app:${{ github.sha }}
          cosign attest --type spdx-json --predicate sbom.json ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/app:${{ github.sha }}
      
      - name: Verify signature and attestation
        run: |
          cosign verify ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/app:${{ github.sha }}
```

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design a scalable, automated policy gate across multi-cloud clusters using Gatekeeper/OPA, Cosign attestations, and runtime security constraints.

- Cosign attestation and image provenance
- Registry allowlist and image provenance checks

## Code Example

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (Gatekeeper) minimal sketch
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8ssecuredcontainers
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sSecuredContainers
  targets:
    - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
      rego: |
        package k8ssecuredcontainers
        
        violation[{"msg": msg}] {
          container := input.review.object.spec.containers[_]
          not signed(container.image)
          msg := sprintf("Container image %v must be cosign-signed", [container.image])
        }
        
        violation[{"msg": msg}] {
          container := input.review.object.spec.containers[_]
          not allowed_registry(container.image)
          msg := sprintf("Registry %v not in allowlist", [container.image])
        }
        
        violation[{"msg": msg}] {
          container := input.review.object.spec.containers[_]
          not container.securityContext.runAsNonRoot
          msg := "Container must run as non-root"
        }
```

- Shows proper cosign attestation validation approach
- Includes comprehensive runtime security constraints
- Outlines practical CI/CD integration strategy

## Why This Is Asked

In large, multi-cloud deployments, runtime security must adapt to heterogeneous runtimes and dynamic rollouts. This question probes policy-as-code, workload identity, and canary governance in one cohesive design.

## Key Concepts

- OPA Gatekeeper and ConstraintTemplates for runtime policy
- SPIFFE/SPIRE for workload identity and identity-based RBAC
- Canary rollouts with policy gating
- Cross-cloud RBAC mappings and policy versioning

## Code Example

```javascript
// Minimal Gatekeeper Rego-like policy (illustrative)
package gatekeeper.k8s

deny[msg]{
  input.review.object.kind == "Deployment"
  some i
  input.review.object.spec.template.spec.volumes[i].hostPath
  not hasAnnotation(input.review.object.metadata.namespace, "devsecops.enabled", "true")
  msg = "HostPath mounts are restricted unless devsecops.enabled=true"
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you handle policy versioning and migration across clusters?
- How would you simulate canary gating with policy violations in CI/CD?
